To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accounting profession is undergoing significant change and that there are opportunities for information professionals in this context.

the accounting profession is facing challenges that require a new set of skills and competencies, and information professionals have a unique set of skills that can be leveraged to help accountants in business meet these challenges.
The roles, responsibilities, priorities and information needs of those with a financial function — especially those working in business — are changing, bringing about a need for new skills.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: • The changing role of the accountant in business • The changing role and priorities of information management • The role of information management professionals in business • The potential role of information management in the finance function.
the role of information professionals in the accounting and finance function.
understanding the changing nature of the information management challenges facing the professional accountant in the business world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the information profession has a significant role to play in the future of the accounting profession.
information professionals have a significant role to play in supporting professional accountants in business.
the information management challenges for the accountant in business are many and diverse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information professional is a key player in helping accountants in business meet the information management challenges of today and tomorrow.
the information professional has the potential to play a key role in helping the finance function adapt to these changes, and to help the organisation as a whole to become more agile.
we have been able to show how the skills of information management professionals can be applied to the business environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

information management skills are increasingly relevant to the finance function, but that the profession is not fully leveraging the value that information professionals can bring to the finance team.

there are many areas of overlap between the information management and accounting professions, and these are becoming more apparent as accountants are increasingly called upon to be business partners.
the information professional has the opportunity to demonstrate the relevance and added value of their role to the evolving strategic finance function.
